entries.title: After Hours Lecture Series: Talkin' Terrapins
entries.description:
Join us for our August After Hours lecture, where Dr. Chambers will discuss some of the challenges to the conservation of diamondback terrapins in Virginia coastal waters. Diamondback terrapins can live for decades, provided the multiple habitats they use are connected and available. Sometimes, however, resource use by humans conflicts with resources required by turtles. What are the issues that most threaten terrapin populations, and what can we do to promote the conservation of North America’s only fully estuarine turtle? Dr. Chambers will present his tale of the terrapin, with a focus on efforts to protect terrapins from drowning as bycatch in Virginia’s blue crab fishery.

Registration is required.

We are excited to offer this lecture in-person in Davis Hall on our Gloucester Point Campus! This lecture will also be available as a live-streamed webinar. Registration is required for both in-person and webinar attendees. Webinar links will be sent in all registration confirmation emails. This event will be photographed and/or videotaped. By attending this event, each participant consents to being photographed and/or videotaped and authorizes the Batten School & VIMS to use such photographs and videos for media purposes.

entries.title: Opening Convocation
entries.description:
Typically on the first day of classes, faculty, staff and students gather at the Sir Christopher Wren Building to signify the beginning of the academic year and to officially welcome all of our entering William & Mary students. At the conclusion of the ceremony each year, the official party leads those in attendance around the building to the opposite side. According to our tradition, all students who are new to W&M remain at the ceremony site with the university President. Then, at the tolling of the Wren Building bell, the President leads the group in a special procession through the portico of the building to the other side, where the new students are warmly welcomed by current members of the faculty, staff and student body. A festive campus-wide celebration follows for the entire campus community.

Not unlike the Commencement exercises which mark the close of an academic session, this ceremony is a time of affirming and enhancing the sense of community which exists at William & Mary. It is a time of achieving focus, of highlighting themes we know to be important to our current condition, and of reaffirming those things we value and share. We welcome you to join us each fall as we honor our newest William & Mary students!
entries.shortdescription: We look forward to this opportunity for the W&M community to come together to welcome all new students!

entries.title: Fall 2026 Internship & Applied Learning Student Showcase
entries.description:
Are you interested in learning more about internships and applied learning opportunities that W&M students participate in? Are you curious to learn about internship experiences and how they can inform your career goals?

Students who participated in research or an internship in Summer 2026 will showcase their experiences and share key learnings, discussing how the experience has shaped their academic and professional goals. Drop by to chat with students and enjoy free refreshments!

Program Schedule (subject to change):

  • 10 - 10:45 a.m. - Session #1
  • 11 - 11:45 a.m. - Session #2
  • 12 - 12:45 pm - Session #3
  • 1 - 1:45 pm - Session #4
  • 2-2:45 pm - Session #5

Contact internships@wm.edu if you have any questions.

If you need an accommodation related to a disability, please contact the Office of Career Development & Professional Engagement at career@wm.edu no later than two weeks before the event date. Accommodation requests received within a week of the event will be provided to the extent possible.

  • Check-In: Begin your Family Weekend adventure by checking in with our friendly volunteers. They’ll provide you with all the information and materials you need to make the most of your visit.
  • Ask Questions: Have any questions? Our knowledgeable volunteers are here to help! Whether you need directions, event details, or recommendations, feel free to ask.
  • Commemorative Photo Booth: Capture the memories of Family Weekend at our commemorative photo booth! Snap fun photos with your family and friends to remember this weekend for years to come.
  • More Activities: Discover additional activities and surprises we have in store for you throughout the weekend.

We can’t wait to welcome you and your family to a weekend full of fun, connection, and cherished memories! We have a full slate of activities happening in Family Weekend Headquarters. Review the complete schedule of events.

entries.title: Marine Science Mad Lab & Trunk-or-Treat!
entries.description:
Dive into the mysteries of the deep at this family-friendly Halloween Mad Lab and Trunk-or-Treat adventure! Explore hands-on experiments and spooky science demonstrations that reveal how incredible deep-sea creatures have adapted to survive in the dark, crushing depths of the ocean. Discover the real animals that inspired legends of sea monsters and famous movie beasts while uncovering the surprising science behind their strange adaptations.

Scientists and educators from the Batten School & VIMS will host a trunk-or-treat with special marine-themed decorations!

Costumes are encouraged for an evening of treats, discovery, and frightfully fun marine science!

Reservations to this event are required due to limited space.

entries.title: Discovery Lab: Blue Crabs!
entries.description:
Dive into the fascinating world of one of the Bay's most iconic creatures - the Blue Crab - at this fun-filled family Discovery Lab!

Discover how these incredibly important creatures grow, survive, and support a healthy ecosystem through interactive activities, hands-on exploration, and engaging demonstrations. Learn about the blue crab's incredible life cycle, and uncover what we can all do to help protect this important species. Gabby Saluta, a marine scientist at the Batten School & VIMS, will provide a talk focused on the long-running Blue Crab Winter Dredge Survey - which helps us estimate the number of crabs in the Bay every year!

Discovery Labs are free, family-friendly programs provided each month by educators at the Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve in Virginia (CBNERR-VA) and the Batten School & VIMS. Designed with elementary-aged youth and their parents in mind, each lab focuses on a different topic related to the Chesapeake Bay and our local environment and includes exhibits, demonstrations, and hands-on activities as well as a short presentation (from 6:30-7:00 PM) by an expert on the topic.

Reservations to this event are required due to limited space.

Discovery Labs are free, family-friendly programs provided each month by educators at the Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve in Virginia (CBNERR-VA) and the Batten School & VIMS. Designed with elementary-aged youth and their parents in mind, each lab focuses on a different topic related to the Chesapeake Bay and our local environment and includes exhibits, demonstrations, and hands-on activities as well as a short presentation (from 6:30-7:00 PM) by an expert on the topic.

Reservations to this event are required due to limited space.

entries.title: Charter Day Ancestral Remembrance Tribute
entries.description: In observance of the university’s 334th Charter Day, members of the William & Mary community and community members in Williamsburg and beyond are invited to the 4th Annual Ancestral Remembrance Tribute at the Hearth: Memorial to the Enslaved. The ceremony will include the calling of the known names of those enslaved by William & Mary, libations, and collective reflection honoring the enduring presence and labor that have shaped the university across generations. The gathering offers an opportunity to remember, give thanks, and reaffirm our responsibility to carry forward this legacy with care and intention. Attendees are encouraged to wear winter white as a gesture of unity and remembrance. Tributary flowers are welcome.
